clue.text: Not that their fruits interest antiquarians

definitions.text: Not that their fruits interest antiquarians

parts.words: Not that their fruits interest antiquarians
parts.note: surface reading: some trees bear fruit that antiquarians find worth studying
setter's reading: the fruits are dates, and dates are what antiquarians care about, but not these ones

explanation.walkthrough: The joke is the two senses of date: the fruit on the tree and the year a historian pins on an object. 'Not that' admits the antiquarians would be disappointed.
explanation.definitionFit: These palm trees grow the sweet brown fruit called a date, the same word as a calendar point.

clue.text: Plainspoken aim of leftists?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: blunt, frank, utterly straightforward

definitions.note: read as two words, what the left wants for its rivals
definitions.meaning: second meaning: split in two, what the political left wishes on its opponents on the right

explanation.surface: Political radicals are frank about their goals.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words, the answer is a slogan: those on the left want the right brought low.
explanation.definitionFit: Downright means thoroughly blunt and direct, as in a downright honest remark.

clue.text: Poet of sorts — heartless — a twister

indicators.note: a twister twists things round, so the remaining letters are mixed up
without a heart means the central letter of the preceding word is taken out

parts.note: taken as written, before its middle letter goes
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sort of poet, cold-hearted and devious.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing the central R of the five-letter word leaves SOTS, which with A is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Torquato Tasso was the Italian Renaissance poet who wrote Jerusalem Delivered.

clue.text: Urgent papers in Greek capital

parts.note: the press is newspapers collectively
taken as written

indicators.note: 'capital' keeps only the first letter of 'Greek'

parts.note: the capital, or first letter, of the word Greek

explanation.surface: Pressing newspapers in Athens.
explanation.walkthrough: Capital looks like a city, as if Athens were wanted, but it means the initial letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Something pressing demands immediate attention, just as an urgent matter does.

clue.text: Nobleman belted fighters?

parts.note: surface reading: an aristocrat struck some combatants
setter's reading: the earl gave championship belts to boxers, rather than punching them

explanation.walkthrough: Belted sounds like hit; boxing champions are awarded belts, and the famous British ones bear an earl's name. The 5th Earl of Lonsdale was a sporting patron.
explanation.definitionFit: Hugh Lowther, Earl of Lonsdale, gave his title to the belts awarded to British boxing champions.

clue.text: Appears afraid to take fish aboard

indicators.note: taking something on board means holding it within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: SS stands for steamship, so to be aboard is to be inside it
the hake is a sea fish

explanation.surface: Someone looks frightened to bring a fish on board.
explanation.walkthrough: SS, steamship, is the crossword's usual ship, so aboard places a piece within it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who shakes trembles visibly, which is how fear shows outwardly.

clue.text: Book for swearing

parts.note: surface reading: a collection of curses or bad language
setter's reading: swearing an oath in court, done with a hand on a holy book

explanation.walkthrough: Swearing suggests profanity, but witnesses swear an oath, traditionally on scripture.
explanation.definitionFit: Courts traditionally have witnesses take their oath with a hand on the Christian scriptures.

clue.text: Got to exist without the club — upsetting!

parts.note: to be is to exist

indicators.note: upsetting tips things over into disorder, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: a mace is a heavy club

explanation.surface: Someone managed to survive without joining the club, which was upsetting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' here only sets the scrambled club beside the word for existing; it does not remove anything.
explanation.definitionFit: In phrases like 'got cold', got means came to be, the same sense as this past tense.

clue.text: Able organ rendering in Indian city

indicators.note: a rendering is a new version or interpretation, so the letters are performed in another order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A skilful organ recital takes place in an Indian city.
explanation.definitionFit: Bangalore, now Bengaluru, is a large city and state capital in southern India.

clue.text: Relaxed, having stopped losing head

indicators.note: losing its head means the word before drops its first letter

parts.note: to cease is to stop

explanation.surface: Someone calmed down once they had stopped losing their temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Losing head' sounds like losing one's temper; it removes the C.
explanation.definitionFit: Eased means made less tense or slackened off, just as relaxed does.

clue.text: Picture of a literary squire?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a film, especially a cowboy film
second meaning: the surname of the hearty, hard-drinking squire in Fielding's novel Tom Jones

explanation.surface: A portrait of a country gentleman from a novel.
explanation.walkthrough: Picture means a film here, not a painting. Squire Western is the heroine Sophia's father in Henry Fielding's Tom Jones.
explanation.definitionFit: A cowboy film is called a western, and Western is the surname of Fielding's fox-hunting squire.

clue.text: They could be grave in a manner of speaking

definitions.text: They could be grave in a manner of speaking

parts.words: They could be grave in a manner of speaking
parts.note: surface reading: things that might be called solemn or serious, figuratively
setter's reading: the grave is a type of mark over a letter, and a manner of speaking is a way of pronouncing

explanation.walkthrough: 'In a manner of speaking' seems to mean 'so to speak', but it is the definition too: a regional way of pronouncing words.
explanation.definitionFit: Accents are both the marks over letters, such as the grave, and regional styles of pronunciation.

clue.text: Play put below "The Cherry Orchard"?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a 1959 play by Arnold Wesker

definitions.note: a description of what lies under an orchard, standing for the noun
definitions.meaning: second meaning: what trees in an orchard put down into the soil beneath them

explanation.surface: A drama staged as a companion piece after Chekhov's The Cherry Orchard.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make Chekhov's play title look like a theatre listing; read literally, an orchard of cherries sends these down below it.
explanation.definitionFit: Wesker's play bears this title, and a tree's underground growth is the same word.

clue.text: Fancied country in retirement

parts.note: surface reading: a rural spot someone longs to retire to
setter's reading: retiring means going to bed, and the fancied country is the one visited in sleep

explanation.walkthrough: Retirement suggests leaving work for a cottage; here it is retiring for the night.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the imagined realm a sleeper visits, a land conjured by the mind at night.

clue.text: New paying guest learns to help boarders

definitions.note: the verb phrase stands for the noun: things that help boarders

indicators.note: something new is made afresh, so the following letters are put into a fresh order

parts.note: PG is the standard abbreviation for a paying guest, a lodger
taken as written

explanation.surface: A new lodger picks up how to help the other people boarding in the house.
explanation.walkthrough: Boarders sound like lodgers in a boarding house; they are sailors boarding an enemy ship, who throw grappling hooks.
explanation.definitionFit: Grapnels are hooked irons thrown to catch and hold another vessel so a crew can board it.

clue.text: A cross on a church in a Devon town

parts.note: taken as written
X is a cross shape
a minster is a large or important church

explanation.surface: A crucifix mounted on a church in a West Country town.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'on' puts the first pieces above the church. Devon is a county in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Axminster is a small market town in east Devon, famous for its carpets.

clue.text: Course in which we're in difficulties

definitions.text: Course in which we're in difficulties

parts.words: Course in which we're in difficulties
parts.note: surface reading: a route or programme that lands us in trouble
setter's reading: a course of a meal, one that also gives the idiom for being in trouble

explanation.walkthrough: Course looks like a route or plan; it is a dish in a meal, and 'in the ___' is an idiom for being in trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: This liquid starter is a meal course, and being in it is a common idiom for facing trouble.

clue.text: American detective of more colourful fashion

parts.note: pinker means rosier, having more colour
ton is a dated word for fashion or style

explanation.surface: A US private eye with a flashier dress sense.
explanation.walkthrough: Ton, from French, is an old word for high fashion, as in 'the ton' of Regency society.
explanation.definitionFit: Allan Pinkerton founded America's famous detective agency, and his operatives were known by his name.

clue.text: Pianist and churchman in the vessel

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a pan is a cooking vessel
split as church, abbreviated CH, plus man

explanation.surface: A musician and a priest are together on a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: Vladimir de Pachmann was a Ukrainian-born pianist famous for Chopin and for chattering to his audiences. Churchman is split into two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Vladimir de Pachmann was a celebrated concert pianist of the late nineteenth and early twentieth centuries.

clue.text: Are metaphors so very hot?

definitions.note: a question standing for an adjective describing metaphors
definitions.meaning: first meaning: figurative, relating to tropes, which metaphors are
second meaning: as hot as the regions near the equator

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether metaphors can really be so heated.
explanation.walkthrough: A trope is a figure of speech, and the rare adjective from it is spelt the same as the climate word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means sweltering, like the torrid zone, and also figurative, from trope, a figure of speech.

clue.text: Book, and how I hope it's presented

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a large, weighty volume

definitions.note: read as two words, the phrase for a gift's recipient
definitions.meaning: second meaning: split in two, the words that say a gift is for the speaker

explanation.surface: A volume, and the wish that it will be given to the speaker as a present.
explanation.walkthrough: Split in two, the answer reads TO ME: the hope that the book is presented to the speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: A tome is a big, heavy volume, a literary word for a book.

clue.text: Cleaner gets upset about nothing in Gwent

definitions.note: stands for a town in Gwent

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the scrambled letters go round the next piece
being upset means being knocked over and thrown into disorder, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written
nothing is zero, written as the letter O

explanation.surface: A Welsh cleaning lady gets upset over nothing at all.
explanation.walkthrough: Gwent was a Welsh county (1974-96); Caerleon is a small town there with a Roman amphitheatre, linked to Arthurian legend.
explanation.definitionFit: Caerleon is a historic town near Newport, inside the old Welsh county of Gwent.

clue.text: Cleans self-starter — little afterthought

indicators.note: a starter comes first, so only the opening letter of the word before is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of this word
wee is Scottish for little
PS, postscript, is an afterthought added to a letter

explanation.surface: A self-cleaning gadget, with a small note added at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Self-starter' looks like a word for a motivated person, but it is the first letter of self.
explanation.definitionFit: To sweep is to clean a floor or chimney with a brush, so sweeps means cleans.

clue.text: Goblins make rings round redhead

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the ringing word goes about the kept letter

parts.note: a bell tolls when it rings
the head of the word red is its first letter

explanation.surface: Mischievous sprites dance in rings around a red-haired person.
explanation.walkthrough: A redhead suggests a person with red hair; it is the head of the word red.
explanation.definitionFit: Trolls are ugly, mischievous creatures of Scandinavian folklore, akin to goblins.

clue.text: Novelist is an eccentric, with merit

indicators.note: something eccentric is off-centre and odd, so the letters before it are arranged oddly

parts.note: taken as written
worth is merit or value

explanation.surface: A writer is judged to be odd but talented.
explanation.walkthrough: William Harrison Ainsworth was a Victorian author of historical romances such as Rookwood and Old St Paul's.
explanation.definitionFit: Harrison Ainsworth wrote some forty historical romances in nineteenth-century England, making him a popular writer of fiction.

clue.text: A very big order in the main?

parts.note: taken as written
vast means enormous

explanation.surface: A huge instruction given at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: The main is an old word for the open sea; sailors use this as an order to stop.
explanation.definitionFit: Avast is a nautical command meaning stop or hold, given aboard ship on the high seas.

clue.text: Mystery writer includes Poles in police group

indicators.note: to include something is to hold it inside, so the writer's name wraps round the other piece

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe wrote early detective and mystery tales
a pole is a compass point such as south, abbreviated S; plural, so two of them

explanation.surface: A crime novelist takes some Polish characters into a police squad.
explanation.walkthrough: Poles look like people from Poland, but they are the earth's poles, each abbreviated S here.
explanation.definitionFit: A posse is a band of citizens summoned by a sheriff to help enforce the law, as in Westerns.

clue.text: Ducky dish

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a dessert or pudding course

explanation.walkthrough: Ducky suggests a duck dish on a menu; it is a dated word for cute. A sweet is the British name for a dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweet means cute or charming, and in Britain a sweet is also the dessert served after the main dish.

clue.text: Children's book illustrator finds a source of soft drinks?

parts.note: taken as written
TT means teetotal, someone who drinks only non-alcoholic drinks
a well is a source of water

explanation.surface: An artist of picture books discovers a supply of fizzy drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: Mabel Lucie Attwell drew chubby, cherubic children for postcards and books, including an edition of Peter Pan.
explanation.definitionFit: Mabel Lucie Attwell was a much-loved English artist whose drawings of toddlers decorated many children's books.

clue.text: A nice varied little part of 6 ac — very old

indicators.note: varied means changed about, so these letters are given a different order

parts.note: taken as written
NT, short for New Testament, is part of the book at 6 across

explanation.surface: A pleasant, varied passage of scripture turns out to be very old.
explanation.walkthrough: 6 across is the book sworn on in court, and NT is the usual abbreviation for its later half.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancient describes something belonging to the distant past, of great age.

clue.text: Confectionary put back in illustration

indicators.note: putting something back sends it in the opposite direction, so read right to left
in says the letters sit inside the following word, waiting to be found

parts.note: the run of letters in the middle of the word

explanation.surface: Sweets are pictured backwards in a drawing.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs backwards in illustraTRATSion, from the T to the S.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarts are pastry cases with sweet fillings, sold among cakes and confectionery.

clue.text: Solitary king's one-way ticket northwards?

definitions.note: a king held alone in its suit

parts.note: a single is a ticket for the outward journey only
towards the north, written as TO plus N, the compass abbreviation

explanation.surface: A lonely monarch buys a one-way rail ticket to the north.
explanation.walkthrough: In card games such as bridge, a card that is the only one held in its suit is a singleton, so a lone king qualifies.
explanation.definitionFit: A singleton is a card that is the only one of its suit in a hand, as a bare king can be.
